I am 54 this year. I have farmed these 10.9 mu in Quzhou for 30 years, ever since I came back home after finishing middle school. My family has 11 mouths — my old mother, my wife, me, and my two sons with their wives and children. My sons and their wives work in a factory in Handan city, so they send money back. That helps me buy inputs, but I still watch every yuan. Fertilizer and diesel for the pump keep getting more expensive.

I split my land into two parts. Seven mu I keep for wheat-maize double cropping. That is my foundation — two harvests a year, and I need the grain for the family and the cash. The other 3.9 mu I plant cotton. Cotton is more work, especially all the spraying, but last year the price was over 3 yuan per jin, and my neighbor Lao Wang did well on it. With family labor around, we can handle the busy times.

For the winter wheat on those 7 mu: I sowed last October with Luyuan 502, an improved seed I bought from the dealer. I rotary-tilled before sowing and put down 100 jin of compound fertilizer per mu as base — that is two 50-jin bags. Now in spring I will topdress with one bag of urea per mu, about 50 jin. That gives me about 35 kg of nitrogen, 22 kg of phosphorus, and 6 kg of potassium per mu. I will irrigate four times from my well: once at green-up in March, once at jointing, once at heading, and once at grain filling. The electricity for pumping costs me about 50 yuan each time. For pests, I spray herbicide once after green-up and insecticide twice — once for aphids and once for armyworm. Three sprayings total. If the weather is normal, I expect about 1000 jin per mu, which is 500 kg.

For the summer maize on the same 7 mu: After wheat harvest in early June, I plant Denghai 605, a hybrid seed. I do not till again — I sow directly into the wheat stubble, which saves time and diesel. At sowing I put down 80 jin per mu of compound fertilizer, and topdress once with urea at the big-flush stage. That works out to about 25 kg nitrogen, 7 kg phosphorus, and 7 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate twice — once right after sowing if it is dry, and once at tasseling. For pests, herbicide once and insecticide twice, so three sprayings total. I expect about 1040 jin per mu, around 520 kg.

For the cotton on 3.9 mu: I sow in late April with Jinmian 4, an improved seed. I rotary-till first, then put plastic film down because cotton needs the warmth. Base fertilizer is 100 jin per mu of compound fertilizer, and I topdress twice during the season. Total nutrients are about 18 kg nitrogen, 15 kg phosphorus, and 15 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate twice, once at flowering and once at boll-setting. Cotton is the hard one for spraying — bollworms, aphids, and spider mites keep coming back. I spray insecticide about 12 times, herbicide once, and plant regulator twice. That is 14 sprayings total. I also have to prune the cotton, which takes a lot of labor. If things go well, I expect about 550 jin per mu, which is 275 kg.

I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than risk losing yield. A bad harvest is a disaster for my family; wasting some fertilizer is just money I could have saved. I watch what my neighbors do — most people around here apply similar amounts. If everyone is putting two bags of compound on wheat, I do the same. I learned most of this from doing it year after year, from talking to the input dealer, and from watching which fields look best in my village.
